meaningInput.objectFunction: Venus governs relationships, creativity, attraction, and what is valued.
meaningInput.signMechanics: Libra notices balance, exchange, connection, and how a shared choice is made.
meaningInput.coreTension: Agreement can look fair while one side keeps adjusting.
likelyObservableBehaviors: A preference is withheld until everyone else has answered.
A shared cost or responsibility stays uneven because naming the exact difference feels impolite.
A connection changes once both sides can state what they want without punishment.
likelyConsequences: The clearest voice makes the decision while the more accommodating side absorbs the cost.
Resentment grows inside an arrangement that still looks calm.
Honesty shows which connections can hold an actual preference.
risks: Fairness is reduced to avoiding disagreement.

  "opening": "After moving through {{priorSign}} from {{priorSignEntryDate}} to {{priorSignExitDate}}, Venus enters Libra on {{entryDate}}, and we pay closer attention to whether interest, effort, and consideration are being returned. Venus governs relationships, creativity, and what we value. Libra is the sign of balance, connection, and how we get along with each other. A shared decision includes both preferences. A purchase feels worth making because it is useful and beautiful. Affection becomes easier to trust when care does not have to be requested every time.",
  "tension": "The cost appears when agreement matters more than an honest answer. We ask what works for everyone else before admitting what works for us. We revise a preference until nobody can object, accept an arrangement because it looks even, and keep the peace after the effort stops being mutual. The decision then belongs to whoever was clearest, while the more accommodating side carries the extra cost. Resentment enters a relationship that still looks perfectly calm.",
  "development": "The issue may be a relationship where the same person always chooses the harmless answer, a shared expense left unequal because asking for the exact amount feels rude, or an attraction sustained by being admired rather than being known. Each compromise seems small. Together they teach others that our preferences can be moved and our limits can wait. By the time a real disagreement arrives, nobody knows which agreement was sincere.",
  "close": "Before {{exitDate}}, an arrangement may strain when the person who kept agreeing can no longer accept what they do not want."
}
